title: Fixed-G1 pairing inversion by plain parallel Pollard rho in GT with distributed distinguished points and a deterministic round meter

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and uniform z in GT, the classical cold attack in proof.md computes g=e(P,Q0), solves z=g^a in GT by plain R=2048-multiplying parallel Pollard rho (no Frobenius/inversion classes, no cycle detector; keys from the canonical exported first Fp coefficient of the blst tower representation; distinguished points (theta=2^-64) routed by disjoint key bits to 2^16 storage nodes, each natively addressable below 2^62 bytes, with per-node caps and charged node set-up; start-replay recovery) and returns Q=[a]Q0 after verifying e(P,Q)=z. A round counter, event caps and capped samplers make W_max < 2^128.0319 dense-Fp12-multiplication units (C=20000) hold on every execution; every walk step is one dense Fp12 multiplication plus 1256 charged instructions. Success is at least 0.39 under the disclosed random-mapping heuristic H1 with a factor-2 margin (kappa=2); H1 explicitly includes pseudo-randomness of the index, distinguished and routing bit fields. Peak memory < 2^76 bytes; preprocessing < 2^32.1 units, included; no nonuniform advice. The submitted rational bound is justified by the exact inequality W_max^100 <= 2^12804 checked in experiment.py. Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: BLS12-381 parameter checks and exact rational ledger/score inequality; end-to-end toy runs of the specified multiplicative walk in prime-order subgroups of F_q^* measuring success, wrong outputs and the empirical birthday constant kappa. Toy runs also route reports to 16 capped nodes and report overflows and load balance.
